doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: His place in history, regrets and what he enjoyed
summary: Carter wants only to be remembered as having been here, would change some missed opportunities, and enjoyed it all.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: As we draw to the end of this six-hour marathon, and just celebrating your eighty- fifth birthday, this may be a nice time to reflect on just some general, universal questions. Do you ever think about your place in—quote, unquote—the history of music and something like that? When people look at the history of music, is there something that you’d like to be remembered for more than anything else of all the things you’ve done?

No, all I would like to remember for is having been here. Whatever contribution I may have made, if any, is to be made by others, not by me . . . to be recognized by others, not by me. I don’t know that I’ve made any real contribution. I’ve done what I set out to do, and that was have fun with the music, enjoy it and perform it and listen to it, to other people. I must admit that I have, to my satisfaction, achieved much that I had not even thought of. Of course, there’s much left that I would like to do, but just what, I’m not sure. But I would just like to continue what I’m doing, you know, until the next eighty-five years.
Well, we’re already planning the hundredth celebration, so . . .
Well, that’s just around the corner.
You mention that you’re satisfied with what you’ve done. Would you have changed anything specifically in retrospect?
Oh yes, I would have. I won’t say what, because there were opportunities I had that I think I goofed, and I can’t blame anybody else for.
What aspect of music did you enjoy the least?
Of things that you actually were forced to do, engaged in and . . .
Oh, things I was involved in? I don’t know. I enjoyed it all, you know. I can’t point any particular high spots. I just enjoyed it all.

Is there anyone that you would have . . . I mean, you played with virtually everyone in so many fields of music, but was there anyone that just comes to mind offhand that you would like to have worked with that you never had the opportunity to?
Not that I can recall at the moment.
